newsitem.title: UK: Ex-Nadir aide to hear appeal verdict on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nadir aide to hear appeal verdict on Monday.

text.p: Elizabeth Forsyth, former aide to Polly Peck head Asil Nadir, will hear the result of her appeal against a money-laundering conviction on Monday, her lawyers said on Friday.
Forsyth, 60, spent 10 months in jail after being found guilty last year on two counts of dishonestly handling 400,000 pounds.
But she was freed in January after a London appeal court quashed her original five-year sentence, which it said was disproportionate.
However the three judges considering her appeal reserved judgement on her conviction, saying it had raised complex issues and it would take longer to determine whether or not it should stand.
The prosecution, brought by Britain's Serious Fraud Office, said the money Forsyth was convicted of handling had been stolen by Nadir from Polly Peck, which collapsed in 1990 under massive debts.
Nadir still faces fraud and theft charges in Britain after fleeing to his native northern Cyprus in 1993, jumping bail of 3.5 million pounds.

Forsyth's barrister Geoffrey Robertson argued during the appeal hearing that her conviction was unsafe on a number of grounds, including the fact that Nadir had not been questioned during her trial via a video-link from northern Cyprus.
And her lawyer Peter Krivinskas said the appeal was a case which should set legal precedent, although he would not say how he thought the judges would rule.
